name: mandelvec
algorithm: same/mandelbrot's algorithm (an n by n grid, at most 50 iterations, the total iteration count) with L points per vector, each lane stopping at its escape (README.md).

skip.mk-wrap: a float kernel: its only integer arithmetic is the iteration counter

notes: The counts are same/mandelbrot's for the same n (the quick checksum is that row's): the vector form does the same f64 operations per point, unfused. Publish size 9000 (not the scalar row's 5600) so the fastest v3 cell clears the 1 s floor; both targets run the same size. Compute-bound, so it reports time, not GB/s. Go is scalar (no SIMD layer).

mk (bench-final, 2026-11-09): std.simd's Vec[f64, L] and Mask[f64, L] with lane-wise operators, `active & !esc`, `Mask.Any` and `Select`, no dispatch: L = 4 in mk/ (the v3 variant) and L = 2 in mkv2/ (the v2 variant, by the variant's sources), the same text otherwise, since Mk has no compile-time CPU fact and C and Zig pick L from the build's target at compile time. The iteration counter of the scalar tail is checked (+), the vector counts are f64 as in C and Rust.
